meta.name: DEMONSTRATION RULES — TEST ONLY
meta.notes: Written by the software team to exercise the Symptom Checker. NOT clinically reviewed. Must never be approved or shown to the public. A qualified clinician must write or review every symptom, question, warning sign, explanation and next step before activation.

emergency.title: Get urgent medical help now
emergency.message: Some of what you've described can be a sign of a serious problem that needs to be checked in person straight away. Please go to the nearest emergency department or contact your local emergency services now. Don't wait for a routine appointment.

questions.text: Right now, are you having any of these?
questions.help: Choose all that apply. If you are unsure, choose "Not sure".

options.label: Severe chest pain, pressure or tightness
Vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds
Heavy bleeding from the bottom, or black tarry stools with dizziness

questions.help: We ask because some advice is different for children and older adults.

questions.text: How long have you had these symptoms?
How much are your symptoms affecting you?

options.label: Mild — noticeable, but I can do my usual things
Moderate — it's hard to do some usual things
Severe — I can't do my usual things

questions.text: Does the pain get worse after eating, especially fatty food?
Is your chest pain happening with any of these?

options.label: Spreading to the arm, jaw, neck or back
Mainly after meals or when lying down

questions.text: Can you keep fluids down and pass urine as usual?

options.label: No — I can't keep fluids down, or I'm hardly passing urine

questions.text: How much blood have you noticed?

options.label: A few streaks on the stool or toilet paper
Blood mixed in with the stool
A lot of blood, or clots

questions.text: Along with the yellow colour, have you noticed any of these?
Is the difficulty swallowing getting gradually worse?
Do you have any of these with the fever or headache?

options.label: A stiff neck, or pain bending the head forward
A rash that doesn't fade when pressed

questions.text: How often do you get heartburn or reflux?
Is there anything else you'd like to add?
questions.help: Optional. Please don't include your name, phone number or other personal details.

red_flags.title: You said you have an urgent warning sign right now
Chest pain with spreading pain, sweating or breathlessness
A lot of blood from the bottom
Yellow eyes or skin with drowsiness or confusion
Fever or headache with a stiff neck, a non-fading rash or a sudden severe headache

next_steps.title: Get checked in person today
next_steps.text: You weren't sure about one or more urgent warning signs. Please get checked in person today, and go to an emergency department straight away if things get worse.

next_steps.title: Get seen today
next_steps.text: Not being able to keep fluids down can lead to dehydration, which can be serious — especially for young children and older adults. Please get seen by a doctor today.

next_steps.title: Book a specialist appointment soon
next_steps.text: Swallowing that is gradually getting harder should be checked by a doctor soon, usually within a couple of weeks.

next_steps.title: Book an appointment soon
next_steps.text: Losing weight without trying should be checked by a doctor soon.

next_steps.title: See a doctor within the next day or two
next_steps.text: Yellowing of the eyes or skin should be checked by a doctor promptly, usually with blood tests.

next_steps.title: Book an appointment soon
next_steps.text: Any blood in the stool should be checked by a doctor, even if it is only a small amount.

next_steps.title: See a doctor within the next day or two
next_steps.text: Your symptoms are severe enough to stop you doing your usual things, so it's best to see a doctor soon.

next_steps.title: Book a routine appointment
next_steps.text: Symptoms that have lasted more than a few weeks are worth discussing with a doctor.

next_steps.title: Book an appointment if you're concerned
next_steps.text: Based on your answers, a routine appointment is a reasonable next step. If your symptoms get worse or you develop new ones, seek care sooner.

explanations.title: A gallbladder problem, such as gallstones
explanations.summary: Pain in the upper right or upper middle of the tummy that gets worse after fatty food can come from the gallbladder.

explanations.title: Acid reflux (GERD)
explanations.summary: Heartburn, a sour taste or burning behind the breastbone — often after meals or when lying down — is commonly caused by stomach acid coming back up.

explanations.title: A stomach infection (gastroenteritis)
explanations.summary: Diarrhoea and/or vomiting that started recently is often caused by an infection of the stomach and bowel.

explanations.title: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) or another long-term bowel condition
explanations.summary: Tummy pain, bloating and changes in bowel habit that keep coming back over weeks or months can be caused by IBS or other bowel conditions.

explanations.title: A liver or bile duct problem
explanations.summary: Yellow eyes or skin, especially with dark urine or pale stools, can be caused by conditions affecting the liver or bile ducts, such as hepatitis.

explanations.title: Piles (haemorrhoids) or a small tear
explanations.summary: A few streaks of bright red blood on the toilet paper are often caused by piles or a small tear — but blood in the stool should still be checked.

explanations.title: A problem with the food pipe (oesophagus)
explanations.summary: Food sticking or difficulty swallowing can be caused by inflammation or narrowing of the food pipe, and should be looked into.

conflicts.message: You said your symptoms started less than a day ago, but you also mentioned weight loss, which usually develops over a longer time. Please check your answer about how long you've had symptoms.
